Submission-diagnostic cleanup

contributor-tools-hardening-submission-cleanup-qualification.Rmd

Contributing · Object model · Discovery walkthrough · Object fields

Supporting record: claims apply to the revisions and environments named below; this page does not qualify a later candidate.

Qualified source: 01bb39ccf8373ae8965a2679ee4813a63ea2d85d. Archive: /private/tmp/sceptre-bioc-cleaned-01bb39c/sceptre_0.99.0.tar.gz. SHA-256: 606363fce32238354fc0d126d79f515973da7c8287ca43b14ce53ce2d00df4b7. A byte-identical archive copy is retained with the qualification evidence. The default R CMD build rebuilt the vignette successfully. The artifact manifest proves all 176 tracked R/native/help/test files match the committed source byte for byte.

The authority is the actual Bioconductor submission baseline, source 21f9ea098b69c444a884a49bc254de711968e3b5, rather than a later refactor checkpoint or the local planning tracker’s five-note header. Original official logs, source archive, checker source and matched-checker reruns remain preserved.

Diagnostic comparison

Exact artifact BiocCheck Errors / warnings / notes Long functions Long lines
Original official submitted artifact 1.49.30 0 / 1 / 3 49 145
Same submitted artifact, local matched environment 1.49.30 0 / 1 / 3 49 145
Cleaned candidate archive above 1.49.30 0 / 1 / 3 45 108

The exact-archive instance gate finds zero new long-function sites and zero new or modified long lines. It retains duplicate function names, maps reviewed renames and enclosing S4 methods, and requires exact submitted line-text reuse with multiplicity. The gate passes the original submission and rejects the pre-cleanup archive’s 25 new/crossing function sites and 363 new/modified long lines. Counts alone are not the acceptance criterion.

All nine remaining cat/print sites have documented submitted counterparts, including the summary-serialization print moved into write_analysis_summary(). The existing warning remains absence of a direct Bioconductor dependency. No unused dependency was introduced. The three notes concern inherited display calls, inherited long functions and inherited long lines. The new literal-range, paste-in-signal, superassignment and missing-example notes are gone.

The original checker was installed into an isolated library from official source commit ca5c23e019dd695b7a5e29286f593a0e9b13639a. Local baseline and candidate use macOS ARM64 / R 4.6.0 / Bioconductor 3.24, with the original hosted wrapper’s no-check-R-ver and no-check-bioc-help settings. This does not recreate the official Linux x86_64 / R 4.6.1 environment or claim submission acceptance. The separately preserved unsuppressed baseline includes a support-site timeout and version/subscription diagnostics; it is not reported as a clean default run. The reproduction script records flags, cache, checker, platform and archive hashes and isolates each checker’s output copy.

Implementation and validation

New helpers separate validation, ordered identity construction, storage backend dispatch, migration phases, proposal admission and complete-family commitment. They retain validation order and the collector’s all-or-nothing result/cache admission. A local environment captures fitting warnings without superassignment; migration explicitly returns the updated object. The distributed API has real public import/setup/assignment/QC/prepare/execute/collect examples on bundled data. Formatting preserves emitted strings and computational expressions, with separate proofs for mechanical changes and substantive helper review.

No src/, tests, DESCRIPTION or NAMESPACE files changed from the preceding qualified source. Native algorithms, scientific traversal, full-family correction and resampling policy were not changed by this cleanup. Runtime build certificates continue to bind the actual implementation, so the new R source requires a new pinned pipeline artifact even though the package version remains 0.99.0.

Full source results and before/after hashes are in qualification/source. The initial older-checker attempt failed before reaching a diagnostic result because the sandbox blocked the metadata-cache lock and network lookup; its receipt is retained separately from the isolated-cache rerun. The external reviewer additionally ran both submitted and cleaned archives with all default checks enabled: both returned 1 error, 1 warning and 5 notes, with the same support-site timeout, unchanged R-version recommendation and subscription-status note. That matched environmental result is retained and is not substituted for the original-wrapper comparison or described as clean.

Earlier package floor/platform receipts and the pipeline’s 38-case/container receipts bind their stated older artifacts. They are not relabelled as checks of this candidate. No push, merge, release, registry publishing or hosted workflow dispatch was performed. Pipeline/container refresh is coordinated separately.
